plainLanguage: Little Elm uses the 2024 International Residential Code, one edition newer than many Texas cities. In the common SF-4 zoning, lots are at least 6,000 sq ft and the house usually sits 25 ft back from the street, 6 ft from each side and 20 ft from the back. Houses can be up to 35 ft and 3 stories. Many neighborhoods are Planned Developments with their own rules, so check your plat and HOA papers. The Town cannot require a brick percentage, but your HOA might. Expect a building permit of about $0.85 per square foot plus a $295 plan review, and roughly $6,000-8,000 of water, sewer and road impact fees. Plan for an engineer-designed slab because of the clay soils.
